scenes.title: Home · what Journey Lab is
scenes.speech: Journey Lab helps you understand your product through the eyes of AI personas, each with different goals, expectations, and constraints. Follow their experiences, discover friction, and test improvements before your next release.
scenes.screen: Home hero: product definition, the shared Gather app, and its different AI personas.
actions: Hold the product definition; point from the shared app to its perspectives.
Scroll to How Journey Lab works by the end of the beat.
scenes.note: Home persona curves are illustrations; recorded outcomes are demonstrated inside the journeys.

scenes.title: Home · how it works
scenes.speech: Define a persona, give it a mission, explore your app, then improve and compare. Meta’s Muse Voice Transcribe turns spoken briefs into editable text. Muse Wonder drafts perspectives and missions, then navigates the working interface.
scenes.screen: The four workflow cards, with Muse Voice Transcribe and Muse Wonder labels legible.
actions: Follow the four numbered steps without opening an extra model-description panel.
Enter Gather through Meet the personas.
scenes.note: Voice input is described as an available capability. Do not spend demo time waiting for a transcription.

scenes.title: Gather · perspective and mission
scenes.speech: In Gather, our booking demo, Alex prioritizes speed. Maya needs a room for twelve with a projector, within two hundred fifty dollars, including fees.
scenes.screen: Maya's saved goal, budget and meeting requirements; briefly reference Alex's speed priority.
actions: Frame Maya's live preview and Personal goal.
Show the existing mission only if reachable inside this twelve-second slot; avoid a separate setup tour.
Continue to the prepared Maya BEFORE journey.
scenes.note: Use the saved Book a room that fits mission and exact source-run versions. No creation form or new paid journey is needed for this beat.

scenes.title: Journey · findings timeline and emotional arc
scenes.speech: Here’s Maya’s recorded journey. The findings timeline marks where problems appear. Select a marker to inspect the screen, then open the finding: what happened, and what was expected. Below, the emotional arc follows the AI persona’s recorded reactions. Watch it turn negative: the room’s rate of two hundred twenty dollars becomes two eighty with fees. Changing rooms also clears her meeting name. Clicking that reaction takes us straight to the evidence. She completes the booking, but repeats work.
scenes.screen: Give the journey video, classified findings timeline, finding detail and separate emotional arc their own readable moments.
actions: 0:45–0:52: establish Maya's recorded journey, player and findings timeline.
0:52–1:01: click a relevant finding marker, then open its finding detail to show What happened and Expected; return to the journey.
1:01–1:11: frame the emotional arc separately and click the over-budget negative reaction (21.009s original).
1:11–1:23: click the lost-name negative reaction (30.355s original); show the corresponding frame and persona comment. Keep the goal-reached outcome accurate.
scenes.note: The findings timeline locates categorized observations/issues; the emotional arc shows recorded AI reactions. Both are navigable evidence, and neither should be reduced to a decorative background. A business hypothesis, if visible, remains a hypothesis.

scenes.title: Fix · design to working code
scenes.speech: Muse Image turns a captured screen into a visual proposal. Muse Code, using Muse Spark one point three, implements the selected direction in an isolated candidate. Here are the design, the working result, and the actual patch. The completed repair shows full prices earlier and preserves entered details.
scenes.screen: Round 4 → Code & checks: original screen, Muse Image proposal, implemented result, and a brief actual patch view.
actions: Keep the exact Round 4 selected.
Show From image to implementation, pointing to the proposal and implemented screenshot as their models are named.
Show the actual patch and configured-check status briefly, then Watch the retest.
scenes.note: The completed repair includes successive rounds. The concept gives visual direction; implemented prices and preserved data are actual candidate behavior.

scenes.title: Retest · Maya and Alex
scenes.speech: Muse Wonder retests both personas. In these recorded sessions, Maya goes from ten actions to five. Alex stays at six. Both complete their bookings, and the configured checks pass.
scenes.screen: Maya's paired retest and emotional arcs, then switch to Alex; reveal recorded action counts.
actions: Show Maya's before/after review milestones and the 10 → 5 recorded actions.
Switch to Alex, 6 → 6 actions, both goals reached.
Keep Code Checks Passed and Awaiting Review visible.
scenes.note: Use only Round 4's exact pairs. Equal elapsed time is not equal action. The numbers describe these synthetic sessions, not human time savings.

scenes.title: Casey · keyboard barrier, repair and emotions
scenes.speech: Now Casey, who uses only the keyboard. In this deliberately seeded accessibility example, Casey reaches the review but cannot focus Confirm reservation. The emotional arc turns negative as repeated attempts fail. Muse Code replaces the control with a keyboard-accessible button. In the fresh Muse Wonder retest, focus reaches Confirm, Enter completes the booking, and Casey records a positive reaction. We can inspect both emotional arcs beside the recordings, connecting each reaction to what actually happened.
scenes.screen: Casey's seeded keyboard-only journey → broken finding and negative arc → Muse Code fix → paired emotional arcs and confirmed booking.
actions: 2:02–2:09: show Casey's keyboard-only context and the environment label Keyboard demo · seeded barrier. Start at review, not the beginning of the full recording.
2:09–2:19: show the Broken finding for unreachable Confirm reservation and click a negative arc point (91.746s or 99.306s original).
2:19–2:25: open Review fix → Code & checks; briefly show the native-button replacement.
2:25–2:40: return to Before / after. Show the before negative reaction, the after positive focus reaction (87.113s), and the confirmed booking frame (87.492s). Keep both arcs and outcomes visible.
scenes.note: This is a separate deliberately seeded test fixture and candidate, not the Maya/Alex pricing repair. The actual blocker is final confirmation, not room selection. These are recorded AI reactions. The selected Muse Wonder after-run confirms with Enter; independent Space verification is separate.

scenes.title: Local analysis · Muse Glimmer
scenes.speech: For local review, Meta’s open-weight Muse Glimmer summarizes selected observations on this Mac. The original evidence remains available for your team to inspect.
scenes.screen: Show Local analysis beside the completed Casey review; keep this supporting feature brief.
actions: Open Local analysis in the same fix-review page.
Use real supplied observations if a factual summary is prepared before capture; otherwise show the available control without pretending a generation occurred.
Do not wait for model generation during the three-minute presentation.
scenes.note: Glimmer is an optional local text-analysis tool. Do not reuse a pricing-case summary as if it described Casey or imply all Journey Lab data stays local.

scenes.title: Close · contribution and value
scenes.speech: Built during this hackathon, Journey Lab turns simulated journeys into better questions for real users. One product. Many journeys.
scenes.screen: Home hero or the successful final comparison, with the hackathon-contribution caption in the final edit.
actions: Keep the conclusion on screen as the hackathon contribution is stated.
Finish on One product. Many journeys. Avoid an extra navigation if it interrupts the final sentence.
scenes.note: Treat emotions as simulated persona reactions and use the resulting evidence to guide questions for real users.
